stem_en: At $298\,\mathrm{K}$, the standard electrode potentials of $\mathrm{Cu\ 2+}$ / $\mathrm{Cu}$, $\mathrm{Zn\ 2+}$ / $\mathrm{Zn}$, $\mathrm{Fe\ 2+}$ / $\mathrm{Fe}$ and $\mathrm{Ag\ +}$ / $\mathrm{Ag}$ are $0.34\,\mathrm{V}$, $-0.76\,\mathrm{V}$, $-0.44\,\mathrm{V}$ and $0.80\,\mathrm{V}$, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
b4_text_layer_sanitized:

At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu 2+ / Cu, Zn 2+ / Zn, Fe 2+ / Fe and Ag + / Ag are
0.34 V, –0.76 V, –0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential,
predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
(1)
CuSO4(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO4(aq) +
Cu(s)
(2)
CuSO4(aq) + Fe(s) → FeSO4(aq) +
Cu(s)
(3)
FeSO4(aq) + Zn(s) → ZnSO4(aq) + Fe(s)
(4)
2CuSO4(aq) + 2Ag(s) → 2Cu(s) +
Ag2SO4(aq)
Electrochemistry
subject: Chemistry
b6_reason: Ag (E = +0.80 V) is less reactive than Cu (+0.34 V), so Ag cannot displace Cu2+ from solution.
b6_working: Cell emf = E(cathode) - E(anode). For 2Cu2+ + 2Ag: E = 0.34 - 0.80 = -0.46 V < 0, non-spontaneous. Others: Zn->Cu2+ = 0.34-(-0.76)=+1.10 V; Fe->Cu2+ = 0.34-(-0.44)=+0.78 V; Zn->Fe2+ = -0.44-(-0.76)=+0.32 V, all positive.
b6_note: Stem renders charges as 'Cu 2+' etc. (superscripts lost) but meaning is unambiguous.
